title: Fooling set bound via monochromatic partition
statement: Let $g : X \times Y \to \alpha$, let $S \subseteq X \times Y$ be a fooling set for $g$, and let $\mathcal{P}$ be a monochromatic rectangle partition for $g$. If $\mathcal{P}$ is finite, then the number of points of $S$ is at most the number of members of $\mathcal{P}$; that is, $\abs{S} \le \abs{\mathcal{P}}$.
hypotheses_covered: S is a fooling set for g
P is a monochromatic rectangle partition for g
replaced:
If $S$ is a fooling set for $g$, $\mathcal{P}$ is a monochromatic rectangle
partition for $g$, and $\mathcal{P}$ is finite, then
$|S| \le |\mathcal{P}|$ as natural numbers (\texttt{Set.ncard}).
